newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon raises pump price of petrol.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon raises pump price of petrol.

text.p: The pump price of petrol in Cameroon went up by about seven percent on Monday following a government decree in line with economic liberalisation measures agreed with Western donor institutions, officials said.
A litre of super rose to 360 CFA francs from 340 CFA, while diesel moved up to 275 CFA from 255 CFA.
Officials said the measure was most directly related to Cameroon's letter of intent with the International Monetary Fund on implementing a reform programme from last July 1.

The fuel price increases would have come into effect last June but the government delayed the measure in order not to risk any social discontent in the month it hosted the annual summit of the Organisation of African Unity, they said.
Many Cameroonians interviewed on radio on the measure said they feared it would drive up transport and food prices.

Cameroon's National Refining Company (SONARA) has been buying crude oil at world prices since March this year, when state-owned National Oil Company (SNH) stopped supplying it with crude at subsidised rates.

Under the programme with the IMF, SNH monopoly of crude oil supplies to the refinery will end from January 1997, when other marketing companies will be able to compete. Domestic petrol prices would then be adjusted in line with world markets.
Cameroon produced as much as 9.16 million tonnes of crude in 1985 but output declined steadily, standing at 6.3 million tonnes in 1993, due to lack of significant new discoveries.
